title: The multiple-of-three branch of an indirect-sum bent family
summary: For odd multiples of three, decide whether a concrete rotation-symmetric indirect-sum bent family lies outside the completed Maiorana--McFarland class.

formal_statement.body: Let $m>3$ be odd with $3\mid m$, and take all subscripts modulo $m$. Define $f_1,f_2\in\mathcal B_m$ by $f_1(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(x_i+x_ix_{(m-1)/2+i})$ and $f_2(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}x_ix_{i+1}$. For $x,y\in\mathbb F_2^m$, let $h_m(x,y)=f_1(x)+f_1(y)+(f_1+f_2)(x)(f_1+f_2)(y)$, with the source's coordinate interleaving from Eq. (V.2). Determine whether $h_m$ lies outside the completed Maiorana--McFarland class $\mathcal M^{\#}$ for every such $m$.

scope.domain: Rotation-symmetric Boolean bent functions and completed Maiorana--McFarland membership
assumptions: m > 3 is odd and divisible by 3
f1 and f2 are the complementary semi-bent functions in source Eq. (V.3)
h_m uses the indirect sum and coordinate convention in source Eq. (V.2)
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves exclusion from M# when 3 does not divide m. The entire complementary branch with odd m > 3 and 3 dividing m remains open, beginning with m = 9.

citations.label: Polujan--Kudin--Pasalic, rotation-symmetric bent functions
citations.locator: Eqs. (V.2)-(V.3), Theorem 7, and Open Problem 4, pp. 4348-4350

progress.summary: The source settles the branch where 3 does not divide m and states the remaining multiple-of-three branch as Open Problem 4.
